chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from Abu Bakr al-Hadrami who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the prey of the buzzards and the falcons, and the dogs, and the leopards. So he said: 'Do not eat the prey of anything from these except what you slaughter, except the trained hunting dog.' I said: 'What if it kills it?' He said: 'Eat.'
Because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: '...and what you have taught from the hunting animals, trained ones... so eat of that which they catch for you and mention the Name of Allah over it.'

key_terms.الصُّقُور: falcons — birds used in traditional Islamic hunting (bayzara)
key_terms.الْبُزَاة: buzzards/hawks — large raptors used for falconry
key_terms.الْجَوَارِح: hunting animals (jawarih) — literally 'those that wound'; animals used for hunting
key_terms.الْفَهْد: leopard/cheetah — used in some regions for hunting
key_terms.الْكَلْب الْمُكَلَّب: the trained hunting dog — a dog specifically conditioned for game retrieval
key_terms.ذَكَّيْتُمُوهُ: ritual slaughter (tazkiyya) — valid Islamic slaughter with naming of God

ai.seo_question: Is game caught by trained hunting animals (dogs, falcons) permissible in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a legal ruling concerning game caught by hunting animals. The Imam rules that game caught by birds of prey (buzzards and falcons) and leopards is not permissible unless ritually slaughtered upon capture, whereas game killed by a trained hunting dog is lawful to eat without separate slaughter, citing Quran 5:4. This reflects a key distinction in Islamic jurisprudence: trained dogs (mukallab) occupy a special legal status among hunting animals, a ruling upheld by Shia fiqh.
